newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cyclone damaged 511,000 hectares of crops.
newsitem.headline: Indian cyclone damaged 511,000 hectares of crops.

text.p: The Indian government said on Tuesday a severe cyclone which ripped through the southern state of Andhra Pradesh this month, killing at least 971 people, damaged a total of 511,000 hectares of cropland.

Agriculture Minister Chaturanan Mishra said in a statement prepared for delivery to the lower house of parliament that teams had been dispatched to assess damage to coconut and other horticultural crops.
"Orders have been issued for procurement of paddy with some relaxation in the quality norms," he said without elaborating.
Mishra said 50,000 tonnes of rice had been released as an ad hoc allotment for the public distribution system.
The storm struck the coast of Andhra Pradesh in the evening of November 6, causing severe damage and destruction in East Godavari and West Godavari districts, he said.
According to the Andhra Pradesh government, the death toll was 971, and 925 people are still reported missing, Mishra said.
A total of 177,150 people were evacuated and taken to 742 relief camps, he said.
